Based on the healthcare Q&A matches provided, it appears that socioeconomic status (SES) is a significant factor in the quality of life for individuals with lung cancer. At baseline assessments, patients from lower socioeconomic statuses showed lower health-related quality of life compared to those from higher socioeconomic statuses.

Studies suggest that SES can impact lung cancer patient outcomes and quality of life. For instance:

- Patients from lower socioeconomic backgrounds tend to have lower HRQOL scores.
- The findings imply that patients' self-reported HRQOL are influenced by their socioeconomic characteristics, suggesting that a more equitable distribution of healthcare resources is necessary to address disparities in health outcomes.

Overall, the research highlights the importance of considering SES when assessing lung cancer patient quality of life and exploring strategies to improve access to healthcare services and reduce socioeconomic disparities in lung cancer care.
